title: Frontend: implement curry()
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind implement curry(). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(groups). Define a reusable curry of a three-argument function (a,b,c)=>a+2*b+3*c. Feed the argument groups in order and return its result. Inputs supply exactly three arguments overall.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Capture collected arguments in a new closure for each call, and invoke the original once the declared arity is satisfied.
alternativeApproaches: Add placeholders and explain how filling argument holes changes the collection algorithm.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: One argument per call; grouped arguments; zero arity.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
